Faz diferença no dia a dia.

AWSCloudFormation.comment:
Basic validation works, I'd trust other reviews that it doesnt have 100% coverage of keywords, I just never got past a few lines once I realised how unhelpful the plugin is.

Auto complete doesnt work. Theres basically no reason to install this in 2025. Sad from JetBrains, stinks of "auto updating the plugin to keep it installable even though no features work anymore"
This plugin works for the bare minimum case, but many advertised features do not work: Live templates, completion, and refactoring are just plain broken and have been for a while.

Works pretty well for most stuff, navigation to your refs are really nice. Does a decent job of showing syntax errors. That said, it's lacking in a lot of areas

It doesn't not know what many of the types are, I just encountered, "Unknown CloudFormation resource type: AWS::SSO::Application"

Also, it does pretty good at figuring out function calls, but I just added a Fn::Foreach to create several account associations, and all I see are red lines. It doesn't not appear to honor any of the LanguageExtensions.

The good: From the versions history of the plugin I can see that there are regular updates to it and the supported CloudFormation schema.

BUT: The newer updates only support EAP version ranges of the JetBrains IDEs. As of the time writing this the latest compatible version of this plugin which works with the current stable version of WebStorm is from July.

Question to the JetBrains team: Is it really necessary that the compatibility range is so strictly limited to the EAPs for such a long time?
Immediately after installation, this plugin found a problem I just couldn't see in my YAML. This was for a SAM template too so it's great to see it work there.
I don't see any auto-complete. It just show what is missing and that's it. Super basic. Don't see what's on screenshots. Maybe it's broken with latest webstorm, IDK

Great help, but doesn't recognize Rules.

My installed version is 221.5591.19. Says metadata updated 15 April, 2022. When I compare to the marketplace, same version number but metadata updated 17 May, 2022. Uninstall, restart, reinstall, restart. Installed version still shows the older date compared to the marketplace and Rules are still not recognized.

Do the metadata updates only cover resources?

This is more of a question than review. I have downloaded this plugin and created a sample file which has default code like below. I want to learn AWS Cloudformation Template from scratch and was hoping it will give me suggestions. I wasn't able to find how to use this plugin effectively or even how to validate templates that others have given as a sample

Is there any documentation for how to use this plugin to learn how to write the CF templates

`AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09" Description: Test the plugin Resources: DummyServer: Type: "AWS::EC2::Instance" Properties: ImageId: ""

`
There are countless issues on how this plugin does not pick up new features added by AWS to CloudFormation, which makes it fairly useless. Is there a plan to automatically import the schema from CF?

Template validation is a big problem. I try and use this and typeformation and I'm not sure if it's a conflict. the

AWS:: types do not show up, needs work.

Have latest version of pycharm, seems to work on pro 2020.2.3 but not 2021.3.2
The template validation for "Type: AWS::Lambda::Function" with propertie "Architectures" isn't being picked up as valid.
It is very good for auto-complete, but often marks valid properties as errors. Needs an update.

For many folks who had trouble figuring out how does this plugin work, like me, check if your yaml file has AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09" at the beginning of the file. After adding this, I started seeing errors with my template.

I marked it one star then found Ryan Murphy's reply to someone's question of his 5-star review. Adding the file association has helped, but it still seems less helpful than the Terraform plugin I've used for years.

Ryan Murphy 21.05.2020

From what I see in the comments it seems people just need to setup the file associations so the plugin knows what files to enable itself on. Go to Preferences > Editor > File Types and scroll to you see AWS CloudFormation Templates (JSON or YAML) IMPORTANT you can add *.json or *.yaml here but then that would make it active on all files with that extension. My advice would be to name all your templates to be unique so *_template.json or *_template.yaml would matc, or make your own extension *.cfn
Yeah, does not seem to be doing much. I do get some syntax highlighting, but the type list seems very outdated. It should be updating continuously!

Nothing works, I installed the plugin and even restarted Intellij Ultimate. References to resources, condition, parameters and mappings and resource types and properties don't work at all.

Please fix it, it will be very helpful.
Does not seem to do anything at all. Does not add support for the *.template, even though that is suggested in the description of the plugin.

Core idea behind the plugin is great but unfortunately it simply does not keep up to the service it is supposed to support. There's huge list of features that are not recognized and reported as template errors. In my recent template almost 90% of resources got marked as wrong which simply means that this extension is at the moment useless.

The basics of this plugin are great. Auto-complete works nicely and it flags issues with the templates well. Makes CF templates a lot easier to work with. The downside is when there are CF features this plugin doesn't support, you end up with a bunch of false errors in the file. In particular I'm missing some or all support for AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup, AWS::ECS::CapacityProvider, and AWS::ECS::Cluster.

Great static analyzer but I'd love to see this plugin get more attention with timely bug fixes.

Some things are just not parsed when they should like !GetAZs

This is what I had to do to make this plugin work: - Settings -> Languages and Frameworks -> Javascript -> Libraries - From https://www.jetbrains.com/help/idea/2016.2/using-angularjs.html: "In the Libraries area, click the Add button. In the New Library dialog box that opens, specify the name of the library. Click the Add button add next to the list of library files and choose Attach Files or Attach Directory on the context menu, depending of whether you need separate files or an entire folder. Select the Angular.js or Angular.min.js, or an entire directory in the dialog box that opens. IntelliJ IDEA returns to the New Library dialog box where the Name read-only field shows the name of the selected files or folder." - Settings -> Languages and Frameworks -> Template Data Languages - Choose the folder/s where your HTML templates are, then click on column Template data language and select your new library, and confirm with OK. Basic functionality for cfc and cfm present. Even old bugs are not fixed. This plugin seems to be not maintained any longer.

This CFML plugin does indeed offer tag and function completion for CFML (caveat below), with their names popup while typing, while tag attributes appear with ctrl+space, and function args are shown when you type the open parentheses.

The code menu option for commenting (lines or blocks) does also work correctly for CFML tags or script.

Sadly, the plug-in only supports CFML changes up to CF10 (2012), as of a check in Aug 2021. I did considerable double-checking of tags and functions added in 11, 2016, 2018, and 2021, and none appear (while that code assistance feature while typing the tag or function names).

In case anyone may notice, while the "versions" tab here suggests the plugin has been changed dozens of times in 2021 alone, that seems to be a bot that is tracking changes made to this one that are made either to all plugins or all of some subset, but regarding aspects of the plugin that don't seem to have anything specific to do with CFML.

It's also a bit sad to see the that plugin name in the IDE shows as "Cold Fusion", such as in Run>Edit Configurations, when adding one for CF. And that feature does let you map a folder to a URL for launching a browser from the editor...but that mapping doesn't take the file name with it. In a language/app server like CF, where often the template IS what's called, that's unfortunate. (Some may find it sufficient to map all templates in a folder to a given higher-level URL that covers them all, I suppose.)

There are indeed so many nice features in Idea (many may love the visual integration with Git, for instance), but I have to say that the CFML plugin is only barely enough for most needs, I'd think. Supply and demand, I suppose (we don't hear too often of CF folks using Idea). Anyway, I wanted to share this to help those who may find it.

If there are other great features I have missed, that are specially suited to CFML, I'd love to hear of them, as would others.

Technical Report — Docker API Compatibility Issue in PHPStorm Overview - BY PAULO COELHO

Durante o uso do PHPStorm em um ambiente Linux com Docker Engine atualizado, o IDE apresentou falhas críticas ao tentar estabelecer comunicação com o serviço Docker. Apesar do Docker encontrar-se funcional no sistema operacional, a integração nativa do PHPStorm não conseguiu inicializar corretamente.

Observed Behavior

Ao abrir o PHPStorm, a interface exibia uma mensagem de erro indicando incompatibilidade entre a versão da API utilizada pelo cliente interno do IDE e a versão mínima suportada pelo Docker Engine instalado.

A mensagem apresentada foi:

com.github.dockerjava.api.exception.DockerException: Status 400: client version 1.24 is too old. Minimum supported API version is 1.44.

O problema impedia qualquer funcionalidade atrelada ao gerenciamento de containers dentro do IDE, incluindo visualização, execução e inspeção de serviços Docker.

Impact

A integração Docker do PHPStorm tornou-se inutilizável.

O IDE não conseguiu reconhecer containers ou serviços em execução.

Funções internas dependentes do cliente Docker não puderam ser iniciadas.

O fluxo de trabalho de desenvolvimento baseado em containers foi interrompido dentro da interface do PHPStorm.

Environment

Operating System: Ubuntu 24.04

Docker Engine: 29.0.2

Docker API Version: 1.52 (mínimo 1.44)

PHPStorm: 2025.2

Docker Plugin: 252.27397.129

Additional Notes

Usuários de diferentes ambientes reportaram o mesmo comportamento no plugin, indicando que a API utilizada internamente pelo cliente Docker do PHPStorm não se encontra alinhada às versões atuais do Docker Engine.

Além do erro principal, foram observadas dificuldades secundárias derivadas da falha de integração, como ausência de detecção de containers e impossibilidade de leitura de configurações Docker diretamente pelo IDE.

Game changing extension. This speeds up finding and opening related files so much. ♥
please add support for configuration per project

This is a very useful tool in practice, but I had to remove it due to side effects. The issue is that the selected tab on the panel replaces the main one. So, if I just need to peek at a "related" file, I have to visually locate the original tab and click on it to bring it back. Another problem is that if a tab was pinned, and you choose a "related" file, the main tab gets unpinned. These aspects actually make the work inconvenient - they introduce chaos into the already sorted tabs needed for work. This is particularly annoying when there are many tabs, as people usually install such plugins to organize work with "temporary" tabs that sometimes need to be opened quickly.

Overall, the idea isn't bad, but alas. For now, I'll just use plugins with custom bookmarks. Where I have to manually organize everything, unlike here where it could potentially be done automatically with regular expressions.

Also, I can suggest an idea to make a group that shows all files used in the current one, like imported files.

This plugin is extremely useful for angular developers. I have a request, please add a option to make the tab names more compact, like, hello.html, hello.css, hello.ts should be displayed as single hello tab with side label |html|.css|.ts

Excellent work.

Can you update the tab design? The tab design should be something like MyComponentName|.ts|.html|.css So, within a single tab space, all files will be displayed. Clicking on the extension will open the correspondent file type.

Very useful plugin for me. I was tired of searching for the .cpp file for the current header file and open it and I am too lazy to click on something to get to it. And even if you do, they do not stack up nicely, one next to each other. This plugin does exactly that. Good job!

This plugin is extremely confusing to use.

It doesn't let you name your groups. You can't simply drag and drop tabs into groups. Maybe I misunderstood the purpose of this plugin, but it seems to automatically group tabs by regex, or if they have the same filename, or it puts all the files in the same directory in the group. These are all turned on by default. I imagined a plugin like this would be just like tab groups in Chrome, but apparently not.

This plugin works really well! I used TabsStudio in Visual Studio for grouping related tabs and missed it in Rider, but this plugin does what TabsStudio does even better, thanks to the dedicated second row of tabs (just like the best web browser Vivaldi), and unlike TabsStudio, it's free!

I do have one annoyance with it, though. When you press F12 (or right-click > Go to > Go to Declaration or Usages) to go to the declaration of the item highlighted under your cursor, it always opens it in a new tab group, even if the tab is already part of the current tab group (for example, MyClass.cpp and MyClass.h).

The same thing happens if you press Alt + O to switch between header and cpp files. You end up with two identical tab groups, which shouldn't happen unless you purposely split your tabs that way.

I'm hoping that these issues get fixed soon, as the plugin is excellent in all other regards.

Error-prone plugin.comment: Unfortunately it seems itself "error prone". I reported a crash on GitHub and was told the issue is in the plugin: https://github.com/google/error-prone/issues/3587

Having some of the same problems on other reviews but what I really want you to hear is that this isn't a complete plugin.

The ability to recognize a refaster class definition, generate a *.refaster file and apply a refaster file to a code base are really valuable features that aren't present here.

Due to corporate firewalled environment the plugin does not seem to pick up proxy or certificate settings defined in the IDEA settings. So during build time I am getting the following error:

Error:Failed to download error-prone compiler JARs: Failed to download 'https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/google/errorprone/error_prone_core/2.3.4/error_prone_core-2.3.4-with-dependencies.jar':
Connection reset

Could this plugin support the "Before Launch" run configuration option of "Build, no error check". When selected it seems to not rebuild the code and launch anyways. What I expect it to do is somehow turn of failing if any errors/warning are found. This kind of defeats the purpose of using this compiler but in one-off situations where you just want to run a unit test this would be a life saver.

Can't make it work, looks like it doesn't even install correctly in IDEA 2019.3.

For starters, the overview is wrong, there is no such a thing as "File | Settings | Compiler | 'Java Compiler'". Assuming it actually means "Build, Execution, Deployment | Compiler | Java Compiler", then yes, error-prone appears there, but when selected the "Problems" tool window reports "Error: java: plug-in not found: ErrorProne".

It would be nice to have some markers in the code - related to problems found by the error prone compiler - I don't see any option controlling it, and have no trace of problems until I compile the code :(

Groovy Console Plugin.comment: Could you please try Remote Groovy Console plugin? http://plugins.intellij.net/plugin/?id=5373 It is much more useful for these purposes, because you have code completion working there. I could help you with setup and usage tips if you want. I do not work on Groovy Console Plugin anymore, because there is no reason to support two plugins with the same functionality.

Is this plugin compatible with the latest version of Idea?  When I try to run it with the "IDEA CORE" classloader I get the following error:

groovy.lang.MissingMethodException: No signature of method: com.intellij.util.lang.UrlClassLoader.loadClassInsideSelf() is applicable for argument types: (java.lang.String) values: [groovy.lang.GroovyObject]

It's me again. Yes, looks like I misused your plugin. I didn't notice its category. I don't make any plugin development and tried to use it as "interpreted java" for smooth development. But nevertheless, integrating as tool window would be cool, I think =) That's why having plugin would be better than doing as you  hinted. BTW, thanks for hint.

As for OutOfMemoryError, it is not reproduced for now. Probably, problem was not in your plugin, but in EAP Idea edition. Scenario was simple: I had my project and tried to open your plugin from Tools menu, nothing special.

New version released - 0.1.2.
Now it is possible to select plugin classloader to run console in. So that console has become fast(since there it does not need to seach classes in all plugins).

Cool :). You are my first real user.
I'll try to reproduce and fix OutOfMemory. Could you please help me with scenario for this issue?

Regarding imports, my intention was to make plugin development easier. So that all active plugins classes are imported in current console.

But it looks like you are trying to use console in different way. You want it to work in the project's classpath, right?

I also use Groovy Console in project's classpath. I just add groovy-all-xxx.jar to the project's classpath, and create Run Configuration in Idea with "groovy.ui.Console" as main class. I think it is quite easy, so probably there is no need in special plugin. Could you please try this approach? If you think special plugin could handle it better, probably I could create one.

Good idea, but currently plugin is raw. First, it crashes with OutOfMemoryError on large projects. Second, as far as I understand, it must import project classpath, but I don't actually see that anything is imported. Third, console window should be integrated as tool window. For now, ancient BeanShell Box plugin is much more usable, though I'd prefer to use Groovy.

New version (0.1.1) available.
The main change - fixed weird problem with too slow script execution. Also script result now is displayed in the result panel, as expected.

Dear Dmitry, thank you very much for your feedback. Actually I wrote the plugin to learn how to make plugins for IntelliJ platform and to speed up template editing with my style of coding. It was good for me because I mostly insert ruby code into ready html templates, so many bugs were unseen for me. Now having some feedback I reworked Injector to make it much more comfortable in use. From this version you can freely use '=', '#', '%' and '-' characters as usually, because now replacement is made after typing several characters instead of one. Please, try new version and I hope you will find it useful now. Please, feel free to report any bugs and suggestions here or via e-mail.

Here are some live templates I use daily instead of this plugin... Maybe someone can instruct me how to release those maybe in some importable format on github. 

ERB files only, | = cursor or $END$ varaible.

%- -> <%- | %>
%-- -> <%- | -%>
%= -> <%= | %>
end -> <%- end -%>
%=t -> <%= t("|") %>

This plugin kind of sucks. I replaced all it’s uses with live templates, and then some. It has MANY drawbacks, allow me to elaborate:

1) Typing simple things like = and - automatically turns into tags. Which is really bad when trying to type the following: <input type="button" class="foo-bar"> as it keeps escaping. I hit this situation more times than I actually used the feature. Sure you can undo but why, when the more common use for me is %- -> <- | %> and I can go crazy like %=t -> <%= t("|") %> etc…

2) You can no longer type %, -, =, # into live templates with this plugin. That’s right I started copy-pasting from vim to get the characters into live templates. That is beyond awful.

3) The to undo is stupid. It needs to be very smart about it because a VERY common case is typing `class=` -> `class<= | %>` -> `class<= "foo %>` [OPSE, backspace, oh wait i can't undo that expansion anymore]

I’d honestly remove this plugin and add a few live templates. This plugin is more harm than good.

Beside "builder copy constructor" often it's far more convenient to have a toBuilder() method which returns builder instance pre-filled with values from current instance. Spring Boot application freezes after calling WebService with JaxWsDynamicClientFactory when JRebel is enabled

Description When using org.apache.cxf.jaxws.endpoint.dynamic.JaxWsDynamicClientFactory in a Spring Boot application to call a WebService, the entire application becomes unresponsive after the call finishes. All application threads — including scheduled tasks and HTTP request handlers — appear to be blocked until the process is forcibly terminated.

This issue only occurs when JRebel is enabled. Without JRebel, the problem does not happen. This strongly suggests a conflict between JRebel’s class reloading mechanism and CXF’s dynamic class loading.

Steps to Reproduce

Create a Spring Boot project (Java 8)

Add cxf-rt-frontend-jaxws dependency, e.g. version 3.5.11

Example code:

JaxWsDynamicClientFactory dcf = JaxWsDynamicClientFactory.newInstance(); Client client = dcf.createClient("xxxxxx"); Object[] response = client.invoke("methodName", "param1", "param2");

Run the application with JRebel enabled (IntelliJ IDEA plugin mode)

Call the above code once via an endpoint or scheduled task

Observe: after the call returns, the entire Spring Boot application is frozen

Expected Behavior The WebService call should complete and the application should continue processing HTTP requests and scheduled tasks normally.

Actual Behavior

After the WebService call, all threads are blocked

HTTP requests never get responses

Scheduled tasks stop executing

No obvious exception stack traces are printed

Environment

JDK: 1.8.0_181

Spring Boot: 2.7.18

Apache CXF: 3.X

JRebel: 2025.3.1

OS: Windows 11

Additional Notes

Disabling JRebel completely resolves the issue

Even calling client.destroy() does not help

The problem occurs right after the first WebService invocation

Likely cause: a deadlock or resource contention between JRebel’s classloader and CXF’s runtime-generated classes from WSDL

It is such a niche use case but simultaneously very important for someone who is starting to use JetBrains IDEs coming from something like VSCode.

This is because you would be more likely to install the VSCode keymap plugin in such a situation, which remaps most (not all) of shortcuts inside the JetBrains IDE to the default VSCode ones.

Now, the problem comes when you want to know which shortcuts are remapped to the VSCode ones and which ones are unchanged (remain as default JetBrains ones). Also, you do want to learn these shortcuts, so you would benefit from printing them out.

It's a niche use case but the fact that JetBrains took the time and effort to implement it as a plugin is amazing. Thank you!

LivePlugin.comment: This plugin is amazing, excellent job.

JetBrains needs to make this a built in first class citizen to compete with VSCode. I really don't like VSCode for a few reasons, mostly the constant 1/2 broken cobbled together feel it has, and the really poor UX. But the fact is it's trivial to write plugins for it. And now it seems like it's overtaken IntelliJ as the preferred platform for new plugins. Jetbrains really needs to pay attention here.

I love writing plugins for my editors (started with TextMate 1) but Jetbrains stuff is just difficult and annoying to write plugins for. That's why this plugin is so awesome. It is what IntelliJ should have had built in all along. It's not easy to imagine how it could be even better, but at least I can do basic scripting of my editor for stuff like "if you're a python project and you don't have an interpreter set, use UV to create a new venv, set that up as an interpreter, and configure the project to use that interpreter". It's really powerful and really satisfying.

There are a couple issues:

  • Very often it doesn't detect the 'com.intellij' package (invalid caches fixes this)
  • Doesn't detect the liveplugin jars sometimes. I've actually had it 'compiling' with no issues so I know it's possible, it's just fiddly. The plugin will still run but it makes it more difficult to debug when it can't infer types, etc. It's pretty minor
  • It doesn't seem like there's any way to schedule plugins to run on startup on a per-plugin basis. You can set it to run all plugins on startup, or none. That seems a bit strange. Would be nice if I could say "run this whenever I open a python project"
  • The docs use both Groovy and Kotlin, and it can be difficult to know how things are supposed to work when a certain example is only in one or the other, since LivePlugin has it's own way of doing a few things.

In reality all of these things are very minor and nothing that would prevent from giving it a 5/5. When something immediately becomes so critical to your workflow that it's the top priority when it breaks, you know it's valuable.
Very useful and easy to use
Super convenient, intuitive, and works extremely well.

🔥 Game-changer for JetBrains IDEs LivePlugin is hands-down one of the most powerful, underrated tools in the JetBrains ecosystem. It lets you write and run plugins live—no boilerplate, no restart cycles, no gradle gymnastics. Just write Kotlin or Groovy in .kts or .groovy, click Run, and you're extending the IDE in real time.

With ChatGPT in the loop, the combo is insane. You can prototype workflows, automate anything, bind custom actions to keys, manipulate the editor, inspect PSI trees, and even mess with VCS behavior—all from a single script file. It’s like having a real REPL for your IDE.

LivePlugin makes things possible that I didn’t even think were modifiable in IntelliJ. What used to require building a full plugin project can now be done in 20 lines of Kotlin. It should be a default feature in every JetBrains IDE.

If you're doing anything custom, and especially if you're building workflows or tools around JetBrains IDEs—install LivePlugin immediately.

Users wanting to install Osmorc into IDEA 8 will have to download and install it manually as long as the problem isn't fixed in the plugin manager.

The R Language for IntelliJ plugin isn't ready for prime-time. M y main issue with it is that the Documentation tab doesn't do something as basic as show the documentation for a built-in function like, say, sqrt. On the R Tools tab, if I type in "sqrt" into the search bar, it gives "0 results". Whereas, in RStudio, the same operation in the Help tab brings up the page on "Miscellaneous Mathematical Functions", including abs and sqrt.

This seems to me a very important thing to have; after all, who memorizes the order and names of all R functions? Nobody! Particularly when doing this in PyCharm Pro and Python having some functions that do similar things to R functions but the parameters have slightly different names, it's non-trivial to keep track of it all. Not having documentation seems a rather basic thing to leave out.

On the plus side, it does seem to run R commands, and on my M1 MacBook Pro to boot. But without serious documentation, it's just not very useful. I'm going to stick with RStudio until the documentation problem is fixed.

let heights = self.heights.read().unwrap(); // Line 47 let mut heights = self.heights.write().unwrap(); // Line 56, 68, 286 Risk: If the lock is poisoned (e.g., a thread panicked while holding the lock), these calls will panic, crashing the application.

Impact: Application crash during terrain operations.

  1. Potential Division/Normalization of Zero Vectors Location: src/map/island.rs:371, src/code_for_assets/terrain_painting.rs:226

Issue: normalize() is called without checking if the vector is a zero vector.

let normal = edge1.cross(edge2).normalize(); // Line 371 let normal = (v1_world - v0_world).cross(v2_world - v0_world).normalize(); // Line 226 Risk: If edge1 and edge2 are parallel or either is zero, the cross product is zero, and normalize() will produce NaN or panic depending on implementation.

Impact: Incorrect lighting/normals or potential NaN propagation.

ai.zencoder.plugin.comment:
We have been using Zen for several months now and have made the following observations:

  • over time, LLM usage has increased three-fold. Whereas at the beginning a $19 subscription would last several hours (6-8 hours per day), now they barely last 2 or 3. His 'thinking' has become extremely verbose and his means of opening, reading and modiftying modules, very time consuming since he tries several methods and keeps forgetting which is the right one he used the previous time. We thus purchased the next level up: $49/month and the following day, for a mere two hours of work simply checking syntax in an HTML and JS file, we found ourselves going from 750 LLM daily credit to 282. Two hours!!!
  • ZEN is surely fast in finding answers, but 99% of our time is spent debugging those anwers! Oftentimes, we had to resort to the FREE ChatGTP account to solve issues Zen couldn't solve after 3 days! So, yes, it's faster than any human being, but definitely, nowhere close to being any more accurate than a programmer.
  • Opening new chats is like talking to a new person who knows nothing of the project, and although Instructions for AI was introduced, it seems most agents don't bother reading it and make the same mistakes over and over. So, we spend a great deal of time on each new chat, repeating the same instructions over and over. Worse than that, it seems like the different agents have different levels of expertise, so whereas some immediately get to the task at hand, modify the modules and get to the point, others don't seem to know where the modules are, what instructions to use to read them or what to do with them once they do finally manage to open them
  • All in all, I would rate our experience with Zen a 3 out 5 and are seriously searching for alternative products.

However, there are several significant issues related to file context selection:

  1. File picker needs improvement - Currently lacks fuzzy search for file paths and only searches file names. When multiple files share the same name across different folders, adding files to context becomes tedious.

  2. Limited file type support - Cannot add certain file types to context, including .txt and .csv extensions.

  3. Missing new files - Newly created files often don't appear in the file list.

Despite these context management issues, the plugin has become genuinely useful after the IntelliJ upgrade.

One feature I'd love to see is a more concise syntax for line references. Instead of requiring line or lines, it could support a format like :line.

For example, instead of:

  • MyMetricCalculator#calculateMyMetric line 142
  • MyMetricCalculator lines 88-95
  • MyMetricCalculator lines 40,52,67

it could also recognize:

  • MyMetricCalculator#calculateMyMetric:142
  • MyMetricCalculator:88-95
  • MyMetricCalculator:40,52,67

To clarify, I'm not referring to the already supported MyMetricCalculator.java:142 syntax. That works great for file references, but it doesn't let you include a method or field name, such as MyMetricCalculator#calculateMyMetric:142.

This is a CMake support plugin for IntelliJ Idea IDE. It brings syntax highlight support for CMake build and run system. The main goal was to make CMakeLists.txt files more readable in Android Studio. It is my play project to study intellij language support. Please see JetBrains manual for more details. Work is still in progress. Plugin is inspired and based on CMaker by Aliaksandr Dubrouski CMake Syntax from cmake.org is mostly implemented. ca.ulaval.glo.sensei.comment:
Simple, offline but useful review tool with clear origins in academia/tutoring.

A review is an HTML report containing a "General comments" section, followed by per-file comments. The later allows highlighting one or more lines. The tool is excellent for small-scale, offline reviews. The readability of the reports is excellent.

I would appreciate some additional features, such as editable categories (though the default are already very good) or grouping and searching in the generated report.

The tool is not integrated into VCS in any way; this can be a Pro or Con, depending on what you want to do. Since the stock IDEA Git-Plugin already does a good job highlighting changes, I am fine for that.

If you are working in large teams and want to integrate reviews with VCS platforms or review with more than 2 people (i.e. have online-visible discussions), this it not the tool for you.

  3. Save previous options selected for quick usage.

The syntax highlighting is nice. I have a lot of complaints though.

  • My biggest complaint is there are lots of errors (red underline) that should be warnings or even just informational. Some examples are it highlights "if request.auth != null" as an error. But I want anyone logged in to be able to access this, so it's very much correct. It shouldn't even be a warning.
  • There are warnings like "docId is never used" but again, this is just how you specify the docs. "/collection/{docId}". It doesn't need to be used. So this shouldn't be a warning either. The list of these goes on and on.

  • The firestore logo as the documentId is too strong of a color. It's distracting.
  • I don't need a quick access option for "New > Firestore rules file". You do this once in a project, and even then it's usually done for you. This is just clutter.
  • A lot of the tooltips have grammar mistakes, are poorly worded, etc.

I'm giving one star because although the syntax color changes are nice, I feel like this is about as bad as this thing could have been. Instead of adding useful features, it feels like you guys just added as many features as possible. And none of them are done correctly.

As a long-term user of both KeyStore Explorer and IntelliJ IDEA I was quite excited about this plugin. Unfortunately there is no advantage in using it over KeyStore Explorer, actually quite the opposite (and that is without even considering that KeyStore Explorer is completely free to use).

My main issues are:

  • Only 10-20% of KeyStore Explorer's functionality available
  • Many buttons simply deactivated (import, export, extensions, verify, ASN.1)
  • Especially the missing extension viewer is a big problem for me
  • All the nice features for copying and moving keys/certificates between keystores are completely missing
  • All content creation features missing (keystore, keys, certificates, CSRs)
  • All signing and verification features missing
  • Format conversion features completely missing
  • Some buttons not working (DN viewer, public key viewer)

You can simply integrate KeyStore Explorer into IntelliJ IDEA by adding it as an "External Tool" (Settings > Tools > External Tools). Then you can open any file in a IntelliJ project directly in KeyStore Explorer. Or you could use drag and drop... So what's the point of using this plugin?

Summary:

  • KS-Explorer lacks most of the features of KeyStore Explorer
  • Direct integration into IntelliJ as a plugin is barely better than using the external tools feature
  • KeyStore Explorer is free, whereas the price of this plugin has been constantly increasing

It takes 5 minutes to think about how to respond, which is actually pretty good, but the problem is that 6 times out of 10, it gets an Internal Server Error and forgets what it was doing, so it has to start over.

When it gets a server error 3 times in a row, you have to restart the IDE. Not once, but 4-5 times. After the 5th time, the plugin loads correctly, and there's a 60% chance it'll respond without errors.

Qodo gen has been super helpful for the work I do in Blazor and C#. Specifically, I've found that the interface is much more convenient to use than other AI tools I've used with Rider. Other platforms generally have clunky systems to add and remove files to the current chat's context window. Even better, Qodo's agent mode is much more robust and does a better job crawling through multiple files and folders, which is especially helpful for creating new or updating existing components and styles in a manner consistent with the rest of your app. The only issue is that sometimes refreshing the IDE window or a stagnant session will make the Qodo window bug out e.g. it is on light mode rather than dark mode and I can't see the content. May need to restart the IDE at worst case, but not a big deal. Great tool.

I’ve been using Qodo Gen for several months, and it’s hands down one of the most impressive AI development tools I’ve tried. It doesn’t just generate code—it understands the context of your project, your coding style, and your test framework preferences. The interactive test generation is a standout feature. It walks you through test creation in a guided, agent-like workflow, rather than spitting out generic tests. You stay in control, while the AI helps you move faster and more confidently.

I’ve tried many AI tools, and Qodo Gen is the first that feels like a real teammate. It understands what I’m doing, suggests clear fixes, and takes care of the boring tasks so I can focus on the important stuff. Since I switched, I’m getting more done every day.

I really like Qodo, and I use it extensively for unit testing, and the quality of scenarios it generates and coverage I get from it is amazing. But few quirks I have with Qodo is inability to make sure if written test is of worth or not, recently few testcases generated by Qodo looks great on paper, but when executed majority of them failed. Also anotger issue I am having is poor UX, when selecting a class to generate tests the chat window opens and it starts but then the UI is laggy and few options get hidden mainly the part that asks if I would like to mock the tests, usually gets blocked by chat window or there is latency in text generated. I usually get around this by closing and reopening window, but that is another issue I have with qodo. Other wise it is a solid test buddy which makes sure our code is well tested and gives high coverage, only if team can improve UI/UX and making sure the test generated will.run and is compatible as part of generation it will be very helpful.
使用体验非常好，能较好的提升工作效率，就是在idea中会偶尔断开链接报错，希望后续能更加完善
Best and easy to use tool. High accuracy and efficient working time.

I’ve found the Qodo Gen plugin (formerly known as Codiumate) to be incredibly helpful in reviewing, fixing, and improving my code. The integrated chat agent within the IDE—be it in VS Code or JetBrains—allows a smooth, interactive experience. I can refine code, address edge cases, or get structured suggestions on the fly. It feels like having an intelligent coding partner enhancing both my productivity and code quality.

I highly recommend Qodo Gen to any developer looking to elevate their development process with context-aware, high-quality AI assistance.

Issue:

When the Claude Code Beta plugin is enabled, Android Studio is unable to save or modify files. Even manual edits (Ctrl + S) fail with the error: "Unable to open the file for writing." AI-generated edits also fail because the plugin cannot write changes to project files. As soon as I disable the Claude Code Beta plugin and restart Android Studio, everything works normally again, and files can be edited and saved without any issues.

Environment:

Android Studio: Quail 3 (2026.1.3) OS: Windows Flutter Project

It appears to be a compatibility issue between the current Claude Code Beta plugin and the latest Android Studio release.

I hope this can be investigated and fixed in an upcoming update, as the plugin is incredibly useful and I'd love to continue using it with the latest Android Studio versions.

Thank you for your hard work and continued support!
Beta for 2 years now. Terrible plugin.

I don't understand why people are complaining, I actually like this plugin!

I am runing Claude in a separate terminal on my second screen like I usually did before, in a Ubuntu terminal via WSL. I can connect it to PHPStorm with the /ide slash command, and now my Claude terminal windows has superpower: everything I select in PHPstorm is shared with the claude terminal window, I don't have to manually @include all files anymore. And the Diff is now displayed in PHPStorm instead of the terminal, which I really like. It did not break my habits as I was already runing Claude in WSL, but it's now improved! Why complain ?? Thanks for this plugin!
lacking of features, it just is a shortcut to the terminal cli
'Output blocked by content filtering policy' I'm building a home screen. An app home screen with 4 buttons. What policy blocks this?

Incredibly disappointing. It is just a shortcut to a terminal window with some small integrations. All of the screenshots show it running as a sidebar, but in order to do that you have to move all of your terminals to the right as well. This seems to be such a basic fix, I doubt Anthropic thinks this is good and it surprises me that we haven't seen a lot of updates in the last weeks or months.

The current extension is extremely disappointing.

A company that develops advanced AI models for programming should be able to create a properly integrated IntelliJ plugin using its own coding agents, rather than providing an extension with such a limited workflow.

The plugin should work similarly to the GitHub Copilot plugin. It should allow users to review each change made by the AI agent and accept or reject individual differences directly in the IntelliJ interface.

This would allow developers to remain in IntelliJ and continue working normally while maintaining full control over the changes introduced by the AI agent.
For the developers who use claude in terminal. The way it shows changes and diffs when claude working is incredible. For my needs its the best claude plugin

Excellent extension! Having Claude Code integrated directly into PhpStorm really changes the daily workflow: no more juggling between the terminal and the IDE. The slash commands in the prompt (/clear, /model, etc.) are a real plus. You can finally let go of the mouse! A genuine productivity boost, thanks for the great work!
a console hijack that isnt even readable because 90% of the space is given to the input prompt rather than the output. No way to resize or move
Pathetic
Just CLI wrapper, useless on Intelij

Ótima ferramenta, mas com ritmo de atualizações lento.

Tenho usado o plugin e gosto bastante das funcionalidades e da proposta. No entanto, sinto que o ritmo de atualizações e correções está um pouco devagar. Seria incrível ver mais atenção da equipe no desenvolvimento de novas integrações nativas para deixar a experiência na IDE ainda melhor.
This plugin is very handy, it is better than the Jetbrains AI which is quite expensive.
Still in beta. No updates since 5 December 2025.

I don't understand why i have to choose between the possibility to use a Claude Code Wrapper in the IA chat that is kinda integrated with the IDE BUT it uses the useless jetbrains AI subscription OR a terminal wrapper that do not integrate much with the IDE and it basically allow me to go to a new line with "Enter" instead of another shortcut.

Do better please, it's going to be really though to justify 300€ yearly if the competition (like ZED) is basically free.
Disappointing this is just a console wrapper lacking full integration with inline code completions.

Plugin Feedback: Plugin Causes GoLand 2025.x to Freeze, Resolved After Disabling

System Environment

  • System Version: macOS
  • IDE Version: 2025.3

Problem Description

When opening a project with GoLand, the IDE is frequently unresponsive and freezes. Activity Monitor shows GoLand's CPU usage remains above 80% for a long time, and memory usage keeps rising to over 3GB. It's impossible to perform operations like code editing or directory expansion, requiring a force quit and restart.

Troubleshooting Process

  1. Generated a threadDump file via GoLand's "Dump Threads" feature. Analysis revealed that the JobScheduler FJ pool (core thread pool responsible for code indexing and syntax hints) is fully occupied; 2.Thread call stacks show multiple core threads are in the WAITING state, uniformly waiting for image resource loading via java.awt.MediaTracker, traced back to code related to com.clutcher. Critical error:
java.lang.Thread.State: WAITING
on java.awt.MediaTracker@55e5bc53
at java.desktop/java.awt.MediaTracker.waitForID(MediaTracker.java:680)
at com.clutcher.ce.a(SourceFile:138)  # Plugin icon initialization

com.couchbase.couchbase-intellij-plugin.comment:
As a tool to browse the Couchbase database without leaving my IDE, the plugin is great. I can browse buckets, scopes, collections, documents quite easily. Additionally, I can launch a SQL++ workspace and quickly test queries, which I can then plug into my code.

I guess what I was hoping for in addition is some built-in assistance in getting started with a project. It's really nice that Capella offers the code samples right where you are getting the connection set up in the web UI. However, I'd prefer to do a lot of that from my IDE, including generating projects, including dependencies (turns out you really want more than just java-client as a dependency). Something like a lightweight version of start.spring.io would be great, where you end up with a package that's a starter project.

Oh - in looking for help, which seems to be lacking, I did find creating a project from a template. However, I'd have expected that to come when I go to create a new project. So, it appears out of the normal workflow. In terms of the template, I'd also prefer a more minimalistic option - set up the basics and then get out of the way and let me get to work building a Couchbase app.

Right from installation, I was impressed by its user-friendly setup process. Within minutes, I gained access to a suite of powerful features that seamlessly integrate Couchbase support into IntelliJ IDEA.

The standout feature is undoubtedly the intuitive management of cluster connections. Establishing connections is a breeze, with options for secure connections and the incredibly useful "Test Connection" feature, which preemptively identifies potential issues.

Navigating through Buckets, Scopes, Collections, and Indexes is incredibly intuitive thanks to the context menus. This in-IDE control has significantly boosted my productivity by providing quick access to essential actions.

SQL++ query support is a game-changer, offering autocomplete for keywords and functions. Exporting query results in CSV or JSON format simplifies data analysis and sharing, enhancing collaboration with my team.

Viewing document metadata, setting connection colors, accessing cluster and index statistics, and the ingenious "Selective Query Execution" feature have streamlined my workflow and saved valuable time.

The "Read-Only Mode" adds an essential layer of security when dealing with sensitive environments. It's a relief knowing that critical data remains protected from accidental changes.

In summary, the Couchbase JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA plugin is an indispensable tool for Couchbase developers. Its seamless integration, comprehensive feature set, and user-friendly interface make it a must-have for anyone working with Couchbase. This plugin has truly elevated my development process, and I can't recommend it enough. Kudos to the developers for creating such a remarkable tool!

The plugin is amazing allowing users running Couchbase in the Cloud with Capella or locally in your data center, or even with docker the ability to mange the daily tasks that developers do. With full integration into the IDE and allowing me to use my Idea Vim plugin, I can now write queries like I want to in my IDE.

Being able to do my daily development tasks without having to open a web portal is a game changer to productivity. Highly recommend for any developer using Couchbase!
Quite excited about this plugin and how fast it allows me to browse my documents while coding, and manage my indexes and queries while coding.

Must have if you are using Couchbase! Very useful plugin, blazing fast and easy to use. You can run SQL++ queries (+use advise and see graphical explain plan!), create and update documents, filter the document list in the UI, see the cluster overview, and even test connection (using SDK Doctor) to understand if you have a blocked port, or even - export and import documents to a collection. Very impressive for the first release. Tested on InteliJ.

Very impressive how much functionality is in this plugin already! Browsing buckets, scopes, collection, documents, indexes. Running SQL queries AND seeing the explain plan, right in the IDE. Works great with Rider.

As a member of the Clojure dev team, I've been using Cursive for many years as my primary development environment. I particularly like the ability to work with both Clojure and Java, debug across both, etc. Highly recommended!

Clojure, being a JVM language, benefits greatly from the first-class JVM support of a real IDE. Every environment (emacs, vim, vscode) has areas where it shines or fails. IntelliJ with Plugins does occasionally hang or pause for indexing. That said, there is no fiddling with configuration files, you can set exception breakpoints while debugging (even in library code written in another language), you can navigate into auto-downloaded code from any jar/library with full language support (e.g. for Java/Kotlin/Scala), code navigation is smart/fast with no need for a REPL, docstrings work without a REPL, and the list goes on-and-on. If you're a professional developer, I can't see how you could be functionally more effective in another environment. I've been a satisfied customer for about 5 years. Pay for it. It's worth it.

com.daimler.doc.auto-doc.comment:
1、doc插件抓取的数据将在开源doc-admin后台显示。

2、如果你想要在本地部署doc-admin，你需要在本地创建文件/etc/daimler/cdiamond/cdiamond.properties，加入mysql数据库的配置，填入对应的值

    doc.db.ip= 
    doc.db.port= 
    doc.db.name= 
    doc.db.user= 
    doc.db.password=

然后在配置的mysql数据库下建表如下：

CREATE TABLE `gd_gen_doc` (
  `id` bigint(20) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT COMMENT '主键ID',
  `version` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '版本',
  `author` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '作者',
  `module` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '模块',
  `action_name` varchar(200) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '方法名',
  `description` varchar(200) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '描述',
  `action_url` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '方法链接',
  `class_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '接口或类名',
  `request_method` varchar(10) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '请求方式POST/GET',
  `request_type` varchar(10) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '请求类型WEB/CAP',
  `request_param` text COMMENT '请求参数文档',
  `response_param` text COMMENT '返回值文档',
  `request` text COMMENT '请求参数',
  `response` text COMMENT '返回值',
  `mock_data` text COMMENT '版本',
  `last_update_time` bigint(20) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '最近修改时间',
  `create_time` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP COMMENT '创建时间',
  `update_time` timestamp NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP COMMENT '修改时间',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB AUTO_INCREMENT=1 DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8 COMMENT='文档';

com.facebook.ktfmt_idea_plugin.comment:
The formatter built into IntelliJ ignores the maximum line length, unnecessarily "explodes" nested structures, or makes other strange things. But the worst thing is that the the result depends partly on the formatting of the input file. Another disadvantage of the IntelliJ formatter is that it can not be integrated into the build process easily.

This plugin and the corresponding Gradle plugin solve all these issues and nobody ever talks again about formatting. It is liberating!

If you've used IntelliJ's built-in Kotlin code formatter and been frustrated that you still have to manually clean up formatting all the time to get your code to follow a consistent style, this tool may be your new best friend. It is the Kotlin equivalent of google-java-format or Prettier or Black: an opinionated code formatter that comprehensively formats everything. It doesn't break long string constants and it preserves (single) blank lines in function bodies, but apart from that, it makes all the formatting decisions for you.

Automated formatters are terrific. Since adopting them, the teams I've been on have stopped spending any time at all, like literally down to 0, commenting on formatting problems in code reviews or talking about formatting conventions. Just get everyone to agree that the tool is acceptable, and let the machine do all the work so you can focus on what the code does, not where its whitespace is.

In software development, even with AI support, mistakes can happen — that’s perfectly normal, and Flexible Julia is no exception. What truly sets a product apart is how quickly and reliably issues are resolved. With most providers, you submit an error report and wait… and wait… until the fix eventually arrives. ILSCIPIO takes a completely different approach. When an issue is reported, the team responds within hours — and no later than the next day — asking the right follow‑up questions and moving straight toward a solution. And yes, this level of service extends to weekends as well. Once the issue is fixed, a fresh version of Flexible Julia is promptly published in the JetBrains Marketplace. At ILSCIPIO, Flexible isn’t just part of the product name — it’s a promise the entire team lives by.

At this point Flexible Julia is the best developer experience in terms of IDE for Julia. The extension has improved at a rapid pace, with bugs and feature requests being addressed at an incredible pace. It's been a game changer for me only needing to use PyCharm at work and at home, no need to fit another IDE into my brain.

Flexible Julia is an impressive and very promising plugin, especially considering how young the project is.

The integration with recent Julia features is excellent, and it is clear that a lot of care has been put into adopting new functionalities early and in a coherent way. Very impressive developer response and productivity. This would be a game changer for julia dev experience.
This is shaping up to be an excellent tool for Julia coding. The developers is very responsive. I can endorse this product without reservations.

This plugin continues to evolve in an excellent direction. With the recent updates, Julia SDK management via juliaup is now seamless, making setup and version control significantly easier directly from the IDE. The added ML/AI hover documentation for libraries such as Flux.jl, CUDA.jl, MLJ.jl, and Lux.jl greatly improves developer productivity.

Most importantly, debugging is now supported, which removes one of the main previous limitations. With these changes, the plugin has moved from being “promising” to genuinely robust, and it is quickly becoming a first-class option for Julia development within JetBrains IDEs.

This plugin is an excellent step toward centralizing Julia development alongside Python and R. Since PyCharm and DataSpell already provide strong support for these languages, this plugin effectively brings Julia back into my favorite JetBrains IDEs, eliminating the need to rely on external or separate IDEs.

Although the plugin still has several features to be implemented—such as more advanced debugging support—it already enables productive Julia development. I can write Julia code directly in PyCharm and run it from within the IDE without additional tooling or manual terminal interaction.

With only minimal adaptations, I was also able to use the Genie framework to run APIs directly from PyCharm. By creating a simple startup file (for example, start.jl) and configuring the Run configuration to point to it, the application can be launched entirely from the IDE. Below is an example of such a startup file:

using Pkg

Pkg.activate(@__DIR__)
Pkg.instantiate()

using Genie

ENV["GENIE_ENV"] = get(ENV, "GENIE_ENV", "dev")

Genie.loadapp()
up()

wait()

This approach removes the need to manually use the terminal, making the development workflow significantly smoother. Overall, the plugin already provides real value, and with continued development—especially improved debugging capabilities—it has strong potential to become an essential tool for Julia developers within the JetBrains ecosystem.

com.foxmock.plugin.comment:
★★★★★ Outstanding All-in-One Mocking Tool for JetBrains IDEs!

FoxMock is easily one of the most practical and time-saving plugins I’ve used in a long time. Having HTTP, SFTP, and gRPC mocking all inside the IDE is a game-changer — no more juggling between multiple tools or external servers.

The scenario-based mocking is incredibly well thought out. Switching between different responses with a single click makes testing edge cases and multiple flows effortless. I especially love the route grouping and collection import/export, which keeps everything clean and reusable across projects.

The AI-powered response generation is a standout feature — it saves tons of time when creating realistic JSON responses. Also, the built-in request inspector and dashboard controls make it super easy to monitor and manage everything in real time.

Security is clearly taken seriously with API keys stored in the OS keychain, which is a big plus.

Setup was smooth, UI is intuitive, and performance is solid even with multiple mocks running.

If you work with APIs or backend integrations, FoxMock is a must-have plugin. It genuinely improves productivity and simplifies testing workflows. Highly recommended! 🚀

com.github.aleksandrsl.intellijluau.comment:
I need LUA for some Asterisk call routing scripts and my Wezterm configuration. My most needed feature was a simple syntax highlighting and marking of errors. This extension delivers both, without any legs or high memory usage. And yes, I could use another IDE, but I prefer IntelliJ.

Back to the extension: It works and is fast!

This extension is not rated and quite unknown, therefore I checked the source code and could not find anything dangerous. I also checked the jar files in several virus checkers and sandbox emulators. Nothing. It seems to be safe to use.

The LSP of this extension is not needed for basic syntax highlighting and marking of errors and can be disabled in the LUAU settings in the IntelliJ settings. If you need deeper inspection then there is a LSP option available that is based on following LSP: https://github.com/JohnnyMorganz/luau-lsp. I also checked the LSP binary that was downloaded from this repository after confirming the download in the notifications. It seems to be safe, too.

At the moment, this is the best LUA-extension for IntelliJ. The only thing that annoys me are those two notifications when the LSP is enabled:

1.) Luau: No definitions file provided by client 2.) Luau: No documentation file given. Documentation will not be provided

There is some hint in the luau-lsp git repository. And there is also a sourcemap configuration section, but I don't get it. Therefore the LSP is currently disabled in my environment. But I'll continue to figure it out.

Nonetheless, thank you Aleksandr!

AgentBridge transformed how I use AI in my IDE

Before AgentBridge, I used the Copilot plugin directly in my IDE. Heavy tasks would slow everything down, sometimes freezing the IDE entirely, which actively discouraged me from reaching for AI assistance.

AgentBridge runs in a separate context, so my IDE stays responsive no matter how complex the task. But performance is only half the story.

The real game-changer is IDE integration. The agent has access to my project structure, symbols, and tooling, so it produces code that actually fits my codebase. The previous plugin had no IDE context and the code quality showed it.

What I appreciate most: AgentBridge respects my existing configuration. Language models are capable of writing complex code, sometimes too complex. With AgentBridge active in my IDE, SonarLint gives the agent early feedback on things like cyclomatic complexity before I even see the result. My code quality standards are enforced automatically, not just hoped for. I review actual logic now, not style violations or unnecessary complexity.

In practice, with token-based pricing becoming the norm, this also matters for cost. Instead of asking the AI to reason through everything, AgentBridge delegates to IDE tools whenever possible, symbol lookup, file structure, references, and refactoring. This reduces unnecessary token consumption without sacrificing results.

If you're serious about AI-assisted development without sacrificing your workflow, code quality, or budget, AgentBridge is the tool.

  • https://github.com/microsoft/copilot-intellij-feedback/issues/1804

the result is a broken developer experience where Copilot loses context, ignores provided files, or tries unnecessary workarounds.

I mean supporting WSL is not an edge case, it's just how many developers work.

The plugin also lacks important capabilities available in the Copilot CLI, such as configuring model thinking effort, but that does not seem important to ms ? https://github.com/microsoft/copilot-intellij-feedback/issues/1837

my 2 cents : after extensive usage, the IntelliJ plugin feels far behind competing tools like Claude Code in reliability, agent behavior, and overall usefullness.

Workarounds such as mapping WSL paths to network drives should not be required for a premium developer product. It feels like the team is following a roadmap instead of addressing repeated user feedback and blocking bugs. Sorry for being harsh, but for a multi-billion-dollar company, the current quality and responsiveness of this plugin are simply not acceptable.

The pricing structure is fundamentally problematic.

Advertising multipliers like “2.5x usage,” and even referencing up to 20x shared pool access for the highest tier, creates clear expectations. When users raise concerns, responding that these numbers are “not officially guaranteed” is not an adequate explanation.

@pamput Lowercase is required for the hex string representing a UUID. An implementation in required to be case-insensitive when parsing a hex string, but must output all lowercase when generating a hex string. Some popular implementations such as those by Apple and by Microsoft violate this rule, putting out uppercase or even mixed case. But RFC 4122 Section 3 is quite clear: *The hexadecimal values "a" through "f" are output as lower case characters and are case insensitive on input.*
The keyboard shortcut of Control+Option+Shift+u is not working for me on macOS Sierra with IntelliJ 2018.1. Workaround: Command+n to display the "Generate" floating panel.
@ basil.bourque Thx for your answer. @pamput : as you can easily use the "Toggle case" feature from IntelliJ on the generated UUID, I won't develop this kind of feature for this plugin.

@pamput Regarding uppercase, the spec requires that the hex string representing a UUID’s 128 bits be all lowercase, while tolerating inputs to be lower/upper/mixed case. Quoting from section 3 of RFC 4122: “The hexadecimal values "a" through "f" are output as lower case characters and are case insensitive on input.” Unfortunately, many implementations (Apple, Microsoft, etc.) violate this rule despite being simple and explicit. http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4122.txt https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universally_unique_identifier

com.github.masooh.intellij.plugin.groovy.comment:
Great little utility to ease the migration of JUnit tests to Spock. Not yet as full-featured as the junit2spock project, but I use JUnit to Spock Converter this more, since it is more easily accessible from the IDE.

Once you've added Spock Maven (or Gradle) dependencies, just open up a JUnit test, bring down the Code menu and choose 'Convert JUnit to Spock' and the plugin will burst into action. It will rename the file from .java to .groovy; move it to the src/test/groovy directory; make it extend Spock's Specification class; remove all the unnecessary semi-colons; convert given/when/then comments into Spock given/when/then keywords, and convert some basic assertions.

Then just use a bunch of Regex search/replace do most of the rest of the conversion. I'm looking forward to even more fully-featured conversion, but this is a great start!

Really very good plugin offering all the features it promises. The auto-completion for test steps is invaluable, as well as the syntax check and the integration with existing inspections. It even allows Ctrl+Click on keywords to jump to their Python implementation, which is honestly something I had not expected to work.

There are only two or three features missing for it to provide a totally seamless coding experience, namely:

  • auto-completion for variable names

First of all, the UX is a nightmare—no buttons, no hints; you have to memorize all these /{command} inputs.

Resizing is ridiculous, the input lag makes the chat unusable, scrolling is inconsistent, and resizing—better not touch it at all.

Next, the /include command has two issues:

  1. There’s no context length information.
  2. It’s impossible to include folders—only individual files are supported.

Finally, code generation. When the results are ready, there’s a handy copy button—perfect. But until the code generation finishes, the window doesn’t even allow you to copy or properly read the output. Indents, font size, syntax highlighting—it all wobbles, jumps, and re-renders, making the experience frustrating.

Summary:

  1. The UI is awful.
  2. Features are severely limited compared to competitors.

Recommendations:

  1. Check out the CodeGPT plugin, for example, and see how it handles window management, code generation, and I/O. Just copy and implement the best practices from it and other IntelliJ plugins.

Arc Tree is an excellent IntelliJ plugin for making software architecture more visible and understandable. It provides a clear overview of the different architectural layers in a project, which is especially helpful when working with larger or more complex codebases. It also supports architects in checking if guidelines have been followed, and visualizes cyclic dependencies. The view can be narrowed down (focus) to check on specific parts of your application. The plugin is intuitive, useful, and fits naturally into the IntelliJ workflow. For teams that care about clean architecture, maintainability, and clear project structure, Arc Tree is a very valuable tool. Highly recommended!

Same experience as others reporting here, this plugin feels abandoned and I'm disappointed it's being promoted as an official plugin from JetBrains.

  • too difficult to use (everything is configured by regular expressions, ugh)
  • doesn't bother to warn you that you need to restart the IDE after every regex tweak to see if your change worked
  • virtually undocumented
  • doesn't seem to really work even after you get a working regex
  • doesn't seem to save it's settings in the idea project files

I've wasted far too much time already trying to get this thing to do anything helpful, and got nowhere.

One of the critical aspects where Ideolog severely disappoints is with its handling of patterns. Despite setting up patterns correctly, the plugin blatantly fails to acknowledge them. The patterns simply do not take effect. This is a substantial limitation if you are seeking to filter and format your log files accurately, essentially nullifying the entire purpose of the tool.

Pretty tough to use:

  1. You only get to configure the settings if you are on a file with the .log extension with an unknown log format. I can't find the settings dialog anyplace else.

  2. Changes are only applied after you restart the IDE. So, you have to adjust the RegEx, save, exit, reload. If it didn't detect you have to try again.

  3. Only detects the format if each of the first bunch of lines match the regex. If you have an error with a stacktrace too early or have an app that logs out a banner, then this will fail to match.

  4. When it does work, it is a bit invisible - you just get what looks like plain text. It actually looks worse than if you don't have the plugin installed. You only know it works if you get the context menu up which shows intents for things like highlighting, hiding, and working with timestamps.

  5. There is supposed to be some feature to "Intention to highlight distance between events (marks time as red)". If you turn on time highlighting intention then sometimes are highlighted green and others red. I guess that is what this means, though it isn't clear what the colors mean.

  6. The "log level highlighting" feature is a pure regex match that doesn't factor in the severity/log level group that comes as part of the log format. The provided matches are case sensitive and only work on lowercase (none of the log formats I have seen use lowercase, even the IntelliJ logs).   Once you get it working the feature set does help you work with log files. If you have good grouping in your definition regex then you can filter on values within a specific column. You can also filter on partial text matches. Unfortunately, the filters are "AND"s, there isn't a way, for example, to show all lines with the GROUP column for value equal to "com.myapp.MyApp", "com.myapp.SubProc", or "com.myapp.Input". You could do a text filter for "com.myapp.", by that would find all matches, in all columns. You also can't toggle individual filters on/off. So, if you filtered on GROUP and then LOG LEVEL you couldn't decide to remove the LOG LEVEL filter, you have to remove all filters at once.

Still, combining highlighting with filters works well to find things in the logs. And linking back to code provides enough functionality to keep the plugin installed once you get it to work.

If you're familiar with Shopify and want to do your day to day work in Webstorm, Jetbrain's plugin is good enough to make it not painful. For me, since I've got most of the Liquid spec memorized and only need some basic formatting and syntax highlights, I am pretty happy plugging away on Shopify themes in Webstorm.

What this plugin is desperately missing, however, is autocomplete for standard shopify object properties. This functionality is supported on the Shopify-built VSCode extension, but not Webstorm.

In the Shopify/Liquid extended universe, there are 50+ static object types with their own unique properties. It's a lot to keep track of, and having some basic autocomplete would go a long way. Most devs who aren't 10-year veterans of Shopify prefer VSCode simply because of the autocomplete. And those of us currently using Webstorm certainly wouldn't mind typing less.

On a positive note, something that this plugin does very well, is syntax highlights and autocomplete on liquid filters. This is functionality that is currently missing from the Shopify/VSCode integration. I am always surprised when my VSCode-using colleagues get stuck on a syntax bug that would have been flagged by Webstorm and then remember - they're using that other IDE. Ugh. Another wasted 30 minutes wondering why assign string = arr | join ',' isn't working (missing colon).

I mix these filters up a lot more than I mix up object properties, and couldn't live without Webstorm's best-in-class Typescript support, so Webstorm is still my preferred IDE for Shopify theme dev. However I'm maybe a special case because 1) I am the only dev I know of who is using typescript in Shopify themes and 2) as mentioned I have the spec mostly memorized so I can live without autocomplete.

A minor note, the color scheme support is almost there. We are missing the ability to assign different colors to properties, so when you need to access a nested property it's very easy to mix things up. The Shopify-built VSCode extension provides a 'color swap' feature that makes this easier to handle.

For example, {% assign id = product.variants.first.metafields.custom.linked_variants.value.first.id %} is a line of code I had to write today. No autocomplete, no color separation, just me and my mediocre eyesight vs a wall of text. This certainly compounds the difficulty experienced by newer devs due to lack of autocomplete.

To recap, again, this plugin is fine. I'm grateful that JetBrains has decided to allocate any resources at all to Shopify development to be honest. It was less than 5 years ago that the only IDE I could find with even 80% support was Webstorm via the Twig plugin.

That said, I would love, love, love to see a little extra attention paid to this plugin by Jetbrains, particularly when it comes to object property autocomplete. The spec is extremely well documented and updated periodically every 3 months by Shopify.

Unfortunately this isn't open source, otherwise I'm sure there would be members of the Shopify dev community, and even Shopify staff, that would be happy to maintain this!

Hello, I’d like to propose a practical feature request: allow separate LLM model configurations for Plan mode and Build mode respectively.

  • Plan Mode: assign a dedicated model for this stage
  • Build Mode: assign a separate model for this stage

Use Case & Reason

The Plan phase requires heavy reasoning, logical analysis and task breakdown, which calls for high-capability, strong reasoning models. In contrast, the Build execution phase mainly handles code generation and concrete logic implementation. This workload can be perfectly covered by faster, more cost-efficient models.

Currently both modes share one global model setting. Using a single model for both stages leads to two drawbacks: compromised reasoning quality when using cheap models, or excessive API costs when running powerful large models for pure code generation.

Would you consider adding independent configuration entries for these two modes? Thanks a lot for your continuous work on maintaining and improving this plugin!

It works quite well, also debugging works nicely. however, there seems to be no way to have Intellisense for the actual powershell command, e.g. I CANNOT write "Get-" and get a popup with all commands beginning with "Get-", such as "Get-Content" etc. In the ancient Powershell ISE editor, this was possible.

Also, it would be nice if I could hover over variables and see their values when debugging.
Nice
Great work and thanks, but I'd also like to create a PowerShell project (instead of an empty one) as with many other language plugins.

This is related to the latest version of this writing 2.7.0. With the introduction of debugging support, I have to say this makes my JetBrains IDE's the ideal option for authoring ps scripts. Before this, for me, it was only useful for running already written scripts, now I can use it to develop them too. Thanks for the hard work and contributions team!

The PowerShell plugin ( ver2.2.0 ) does NOT work on PyCharm 2023.2.3 ( Community Edition - Build #PC-232.10072.31, built on October 12, 2023 ) on Windows 11 ( ver10.0.22621 Build 22621 ). It's happening the same issue for Intellij IDEA 2023.2.3 ( Community Edition - Build #IC-232.10072.27, built on October 11, 2023 ). Please advise if there is a workaround solution or other ways. Many thanks !!

The plugin does not support Powershell 7.1+ even partially. It fails every now and then with even basic work. At the very least it can show structure and allow code style modifications to a limited extent.
Looks good, but how do you set environment variables in the run / debug window? I can't see any options for it. I've had to test scripts on the terminal rather than in the IDE https://chairarea.com/

Overall it works great, but it has some bugs. It have not been updated for a year according to GitHub, the main developer have not been in GitHub for almost 8 months.

is this dead?

Excellent for linting and running Powershell scripts. Could be further improved with:

  • Updated icons
  • Autodetect Powershell installations, specifically Powershell 7
Nice plugin. It even allows you to create a scratch file. The only thing I'm missing is the possibility to send the current line (or selected line) to the build-in terminal.

Crashes on launch on (presumably) environments that are not Windows.

It would be nice if it didn't do that. It would be even nicer if we could get Intellisense working without Windows.

Love it, really nice!

Unfortunately, the run terminal doesn't seem to support the use of $PSCmdlet.ShouldContinue / ShouldProcess - it prints nothing and the script just hangs.
Nice one. Would be great to have ability to use it with PowerShell 7. For example: now it does not support & operator though it is available in version 7.
Crashes on startup
I miss the debug configuration
This does not work on Goland 2021.2 (linux). It crashes Goland on start up.
Works well for Powershell Classic, but doesn't seem to support changing the powershell executable to have it run powershell core scripts.

Nice one. Could do with some better integration with IntelliSense and syntax highlighting but just a nice to have. The main blocker is not being able to choose which version of powershell to run is rough. Need Powershell 7 support or just to be able to point the Run Configurations at the Powershell 7 exe.

Thanks for the plugin! If you manage to get Powershell 7 in Run Configs happy to change to a 5

Looks good, but how do you set environment variables in the run / debug window? I can't see any options for it.
I've had to test scripts on the terminal rather than in the IDE

Just starting in with Rider and developing PowerShell scripts using that (since we've lost the PowerShell IDE for now at least).

I see that if I run a script, the Run tab opens and shows C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe as the version to which my script is passed. Ideally, I'd like this to default to PowerShell 7 (the same as I've configured Rider to use as its Terminal).

Is that something I can adjust in an underlying file? I don't see any option in the Run Configuration to set a different version of PowerShell.

Many thanks indeed for your valuable contribution.

To make (cmd/windows key) key mappable in Ubuntu (Gnome 3), you have to install & run gnome-tweaks tool, and go to Keyboard & Mouse -> Additional Layout settings. There should you modify this:

  • Alt/Win key behavior set to Meta is mapped to Left Win
  • If you have smaller (without numeric keys) keyboard, set Miscellaneous compatibility options to Default numeric keypad keys - to disable automatic enabling Num Keys which makes smaller Apple keyboard unusable in system.

Now you can map your (Win, CMD) key to PHPStorm. I recommend to disable all useless shortcuts in Gnome shortcuts (Ubuntu settings) to not interfere with PHPStorm.
