org.localization4idea.fr.comment:
I would also like to point out that I fully share jeromelacroix75’s assessment. As someone who has been using your tools for many years, I consider it perfectly legitimate to pay an annual license fee for IDEs as advanced, powerful and well-designed as yours, and I would like to thank your teams for the quality of the work they deliver.

However, in 2025, I find it very hard to accept that there is still no native and free support for major languages such as French (FR), Spanish (ES), German (DE), Italian (IT), Russian (RU), Portuguese (PT), Hungarian (HU) or Czech (CZ) directly in your IDEs. Offloading this responsibility entirely onto third-party paid plugins, poorly maintained, designed primarily to “scrape” a few euros with no real quality standards, and whose authors do not even consistently master the target language, gives the impression of a clumsy, opportunistic system and, frankly, one that is unworthy of a professional ecosystem. We end up dealing with low-level pseudo-developers, outright “pieces of shit” more motivated by the prospect of monetising a rough plugin than by any desire to provide a real service to users.

This gap is all the more difficult to understand given that the installer offers Chinese, Japanese and Korean language packs right from the start, while these widely used European languages are completely absent from the native offering. In practice, this results in partial or outdated translations, incompatibilities with each new release and a fragmented experience, far below the standard one is entitled to expect from an editor of your calibre. Localisation should be a core, robust and integrated service, not an unreliable “add-on” pushed through paid plugins that are irregularly updated.

Indirectly, the simple fact that I ended up creating a new account instead of directly renewing my license, just to get another 30-day trial period, says a lot: I felt the need to compare, in real conditions, your IDEs against solutions like Visual Studio Code which provide this type of basic localisation features natively, officially and free of charge, without having to rely on dubious plugins. That comparison clearly does not work in your favour on this specific point, even though your overall technical level is far superior.

In short: quite a scam.

org.localization4idea.fr.comment:
Critical review of JetBrains and translation plugin management

As a long-time user of JetBrains solutions, it's disappointing to find serious shortcomings in their marketplace management and language support policy. These shortcomings undermine the overall quality of the user experience and raise questions about the company's commitment to its customers.

Firstly, plugin management on the JetBrains marketplace is sorely lacking in control and monitoring. For example, one plugin promising a perpetual license with updates seems not to be living up to its promises: at version 2025.1.1 of PHPStorm, this plugin still only translates version 2024.3.0.

This reflects a blatant failure to update, leaving users in a situation of dissatisfaction and frustration. Stricter supervision on the part of JetBrains is essential to guarantee the seriousness of its offerings and preserve user confidence.

Secondly, it is regrettable that JetBrains does not natively offer translations for its applications, including for paid tools, whereas free alternatives such as Visual Studio Code include such features as standard. In a context where AI-assisted translation technologies are widely available, this absence is hard to justify. It highlights a certain neglect of the needs of international users.

Finally, delegating translation to third-party plugins that are not regularly updated is an unprofessional and inappropriate solution. It means forcing users to depend on unreliable tools instead of offering them a robust, integrated solution. JetBrains needs to rethink its strategy and take direct charge of translations, treating this service as standard and not as an option.

In conclusion, these shortcomings are detrimental to the image of excellence that JetBrains aspires to project. Addressing these issues quickly and proactively is essential to maintaining a user experience in line with legitimate customer expectations. It is crucial that the company demonstrate a tangible commitment to improvement, in line with the standards it claims to uphold.

ru.artyushov.comment:
Excellent experience. I'm sure any limitations will be addressed as the plugin is being actively maintained (v1.6 as of September 2024).

The people who have run into the exception lacking benchmarks are likely NOT adding the JMH generator for annotations. You need both the core and the annotation generator libraries in your project in order to run JMH. I initially had the same error and after adding the second library it worked (whether you are using a standard IntelliJ project, gradle or maven you need BOTH).

Ignore the 1 star reviewers with META-INF/BenchmarkList resources missing. This problem is a setup problem and nothing to do with the plugin. If they expected the plugin to do that work for them that is NOT what the plugin is for.

  • Override tabs Text color: it would be great if one could define that only the 'Selected tab Text color' will be changed, but if a tab is not selected, then the original Text color is used. That's because IntelliJ can set the tab Text Color depending on the file type, e.g. green for resources, white for have files, .etc. and therefore it's bad if all tab Texts are in the sam color. But changing just the 'Selected tab Text color' is very useful, otherwise it happens that the Selected tab text is not readable because of the default text color and the highlighted Tab background color.
